lots.guide_summary: Nothing is the same item. Close entries are all Gowans SOLD hammers for small odd or scrap 9ct pieces, $110 to $370 (single 9ct earring $110, 1.9g mixed $130, 5.5g scrap $370); category guides at $130-$220 sold, plus two passed-in small odd 9ct lots (UNSOLD). No asking prices kept. All AUD, no conversion. Melt (not a sale): spot gold USD 4,144.20/oz (gold-api.com, 2026-10-14) x 1.4328 AUD per USD (open.er-api.com, 2026-10-14) = about AUD 191/g fine, so 9ct (37.5%) melts at about AUD 72/g before refiner margin.
lots.working: No same-item SOLD evidence, and the gold weight and carat are unverified (no legible hallmark in the single photo, the titled brooch is not shown, and the pendant stone is imitation or crushed chips), so both maximums are 0. For the viewing: Gowans weighed 9ct scrap has hammered about $42-68/g gross ($370 for 5.5g, $220 for 4.3g mixed, $130 for 1.9g, $150 for 3.6g with base pins). Melt is about $72/g of 9ct, so a refiner at about 85% pays roughly $60/g. If Gowans confirms a weight W grams of marked 9ct (excluding the pendant stone), a sensible ceiling is about W x $50 hammer (all-in W x $60, near refiner value). At a guessed 5-7g that is $250-350 hammer, but this is a guess until weighed.
lots.confidence_reason: Single photo, no hallmark read, no weight, a titled piece (brooch) not visible, and the comparators are mixed lots, not the same items.
lots.key_photo_findings: Only one photo. Mizpah half reads 'PAH' and the Genesis XXXI 49 verse; a small mark near the lower edge looks like '1ST' or similar, not a clear 9CT/375. Hoop earring is a large twisted-wire design, possibly hollow. One stud has an empty bezel, the other a tiny red stone. Pendant: clear dome over a blue upper area with a lower layer of loose coloured flakes, consistent with crushed opal chips or glitter, not a solid or triplet opal. No brooch in shot.
lots.condition: Odd and broken pieces: half medallion (designed split), single earring, studs missing partners and a stone, pendant in rope bezel with surface wear. Essentially a scrap-gold lot if 9ct is confirmed.
lots.question_for_gowans: Could you give the total weight of the gold items (excluding the pendant stone), confirm which pieces are marked 9ct or 375 (especially the Mizpah half and the large hoop earring), and show or describe the brooch mentioned in the title? Is the pendant stone opal or an imitation?
